task.title: Bind pending schedule transitions to exact revisions
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/813 by preventing stale pending observers from cancelling or claiming newer recovery state.
acceptance_criteria: Require an exact expected revision for pending cancellation and claiming.
Validate revision evidence before lifecycle-state or due-cutoff interpretation.
Preserve typed expected/current revision conflicts without appending a cancellation or claim event.
Keep revision evidence separate from permission, worker, lease, clock, liveness, dispatch, and execution authority.

attempts.diagnostic: New integration tests failed to compile because cancel and claim accepted no expected revision.
attempts.patch: Added claim/release ABA tests proving an earlier pending observer cannot cancel or claim the recovered pending revision.

attempts.diagnostic: Reloading by schedule ID allowed a stale observer to act on whichever pending revision happened to be current.
attempts.patch: Required exact revisions for cancel and claim, validated them before state and cutoff checks, and used them for guarded appends and race evidence.

attempts.diagnostic: The automatic CodeRabbit review remained pending after local and hosted quality gates completed, so auto-merge stayed unarmed until substantive review finished.
attempts.patch: The completed walkthrough reviewed all five changed files, found no actionable issue, and confirmed the linked scope and authority exclusions.

outcome.summary: Every one-shot schedule mutation now identifies the exact persisted lifecycle observation it is authorized to change.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo test --locked -p vela-kernel --test schedule_store

lessons: Optimistic concurrency should cover every mutation, not only transitions that appear operationally expensive.
Check stale revisions before due cutoffs or lifecycle state so callers receive evidence about the actual authority mismatch.
Race-time append conflicts and preflight stale observations should share one typed expected/current revision contract.
A pending state can recur after recovery, so state equality alone cannot prevent ABA consumption.
